parsed.root_cause: The loop condition 'i <= items.length' causes the index to reach 3, which is out of bounds for an array of length 3, resulting in undefined.
parsed.explanation: The loop was trying to access a fourth item that didn't exist because the condition used 'less than or equal to'. I changed it to 'less than' so the loop stops correctly at the last valid position in the array. This prevents the code from trying to perform an action on 'undefined' [a value that represents the absence of data].
steps: Check the array length using console.log(items.length).
Remember that array positions start at 0 and end at length - 1.
Use a 'less than' (<) operator instead of 'less than or equal to' (<=) when looping through arrays.
parsed.tip: Always use 'i < array.length' to safely iterate through every item in a list.
